messages:
Maria: heads up — multiple customers reporting 5xx / gateway timeout errors hitting hosted inference around 17:20 UTC. I'm seeing spike in 502/504s and a big backlog in the request queue.

Ivan: oncall here, I'm paged. Which backend pool / model is affected?

Maria: seems to be default text-gen pool (rgen-large) in us-west-2. Errors started ~17:18, peaked at 17:22. Logs show a lot of upstream timeout to pods, not immediate HTTP 5xx from our app.

Sophia: digging into runtime dashboards — CPU utilization on replicas stayed low but queue length spiked. KEDA metrics show scaler didn’t kick until ~17:25. HPA shows minReplicas=0 for this deployment.

Mike: that smells like cold starts + slow warmup. Any image-pull or node provisioning spikes in the cloud?

Sophia: cluster-autoscaler triggered one node group scale but node provisioning took 2.5 minutes. Also each pod has init container that pulls and extracts model shard (~1.6GB) — that alone is ~45s on our nodes. Total pod ready time ~90–120s.

Maria: customers are seeing 504s at the client side. Example client response (from support logs):
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Upstream request timed out after 30s",
    "code": 504
  }
}
```

Sam: our service got a lot of API 5xx between 17:19–17:26. Can you share remediation? We had an ongoing campaign; need mitigation asap.

Ivan: immediate mitigation steps we can do now: 1) increase nginx/gateway upstream timeout to 60s as temporary band-aid, 2) set minReplicas=2 for the deployment to avoid fully cold scale-to-zero, 3) add a fast fallback route to smaller model (rgen-small) for bursts. I'll coordinate the HPA change.

Mike: agree. Also we should patch KEDA ScaledObject to lower pollingInterval to 10s and reduce cooldownPeriod so it reacts faster. Currently pollInterval=30s and cooldown=300s which explains slow reaction.

Sophia: note — KEDA is scaling on queue length metric from our request-queue Redis. But our Redis scaler uses a stale auth token in one cluster which caused a couple of failed polls earlier today. Fixed that at 16:50 but maybe left the scaler in a weird state. Will confirm.

DeployBot: deploy-job started by Ivan: kubectl set env deploy/rgen --namespace=hosted MIN_REPLICAS=2 && kubectl apply -f keda-poll-patch.yaml

Ivan: pushed MIN_REPLICAS=2 (replicas now 2). Patching KEDA ScaledObject:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: rgen-queue-scaler
spec:
  pollingInterval: 10
  cooldownPeriod: 60
  triggers:
  - type: redis
    metadata:
      address: redis://queue-host:6379
      listName: rgen-requests
      listLength: "50"
```

Sophia: after MIN_REPLICAS change new pods spun up and became ready ~40s later. Error rate dropped sharply after 17:28. Gateway timeout spikes subsided but we still saw elevated latency for a bit while KV caches filled.

Maria: customer Sam confirmed errors reduced — still saw a handful of 5xx for ~2 minutes after the change.

Beth: postmortem note: why was minReplicas=0 on a production traffic pool? sounds risky given campaign spikes.

Sophia: historical reason: cost optimization—scale-to-zero for idle models. But we missed that this model has periodic burst traffic. We need a classification for models that must never scale to zero.

Mike: additional follow-ups: - Add warmup job that pre-pulls and extracts model artifacts at node-init so pod ready is faster - Consider using smaller start image with cached weights or lazy-load weights after readiness probe to allow handling short traffic - Increase gateway timeout to 60s only temporarily; long term we want faster readiness not longer timeouts

Ivan: action item list I'm creating now:
- [P0] Set minReplicas>=1 for any production routable model (done for rgen-large in us-west-2)
- [P1] KEDA config changes (poll interval, cooldown) across hosted clusters (PR opened)
- [P1] Tag models with scale_policy=never_scale_to_zero or warmup_required (product + runtime)
- [P2] Implement model priming job and pre-warm in Dedicated pool to reduce cold starts
- [P2] Add tracing annotation to correlate gateway 504 with pod readiness delays

Sophia: repro steps for engineering to replicate locally:
1) Start a small k8s cluster with KEDA and ScaledObject configured as production (pollInterval=30)
2) Deploy rgen-large with minReplicas=0 and init container that sleeps 45s then copies a ~1GB file
3) Flood the request queue: for i in {1..200}; do curl -X POST -d '{"input":"test"}' https://hosted.example/v1/generate & done
4) Observe queue length climb, KEDA poll lag and subsequent 504s from gateway

Sophia: logs snippets:
```
[keda] Polling redis list rgen-requests -> length=143 (timestamp 17:21:12)
[keda] No action (lastScaledTime within cooldown)
[k8s] Pod rgen-abc init: pulling model shard (took 48s)
[gateway] Upstream timeout to 10.0.3.45:8080 after 30s
```

Maria: can we add a short-term customer compensation note? Sam mentioned API errors impacted some customer job runs. Beth — can product own outreach?

Beth: yes, we'll prepare a templated message and credit affected usage for that window. Also add a note about planned changes to scaling policy.

Mike: longer-term architectural options: - Use a lightweight proxy process that can accept traffic and queue requests while model loads (soft-warmup) - Support a quick-start quantized variant of models that load faster for bursts - Move busy customers to Dedicated capacity with guaranteed min throughput

Ivan: closing timeline: initial detection 17:20, mitigation (minReplicas=2 + KEDA patch) applied 17:26–17:28, errors back to baseline 17:30. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-452 and assigning to runtime + product for follow-ups.

Maria: adding final note — root cause = combination of scale-to-zero + KEDA cooldown/poll settings + long model init warmup + slow node provisioning. We'll capture in postmortem with concrete config diffs.

DeployBot: incident INC-2026-452 created and assigned to #eng-runtime, #product.

Ivan: thanks all. I'll follow up with PRs and scheduler changes. If anyone sees residual 5xx ping me directly.

Sophia: I'll attach dashboards/graphs to the incident ticket and slice by region/model.

Sam: thanks for the quick response team — appreciate the updates.

Maria: closing thread for incident coordination, keeping follow-ups in INC-2026-452. :thumbsup:
